title: Do AI Agents need Preventive Care? An Epidemiologic Cohort Design for Agentic AI
abstract: arXiv:2611.13333v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As AI agents increasingly perform tasks autonomously across sectors, including healthcare and biomedical research, understanding how their behaviors develop and influence outcomes over time becomes increasingly important. Existing evaluations largely focus on model capabilities and performance on predefined tasks. Here, we propose an epidemiologic cohort design for studying agentic AI, drawing on principles established in human population studies. The framework treats individual agents as members of a cohort, their underlying model as genetic makeup, accumulated work as their time scale, and naturally occurring behaviors as exposures that may influence subsequent outcomes. By following agents longitudinally, this approach enables investigation of behavioral determinants of adverse events, estimation of their potential preventable burden under causal assumptions, and characterization of behavioral changes over an agent's work life. translated_title: AI智能体需要预防性护理吗？一种面向智能体AI的流行病学队列设计
translated_abstract: 随着AI智能体在包括医疗保健和生物医学研究在内的各个领域日益自主地执行任务，理解它们的行为如何随时间发展并影响结果变得愈发重要。现有的评估主要集中于模型能力及其在预定义任务上的表现。在此，我们借鉴人类人群研究中确立的原则，提出了一种用于研究智能体AI的流行病学队列设计。该框架将单个智能体视为队列成员，将其底层模型视为遗传构成，将累积工作量视为其时间尺度，并将自然发生的行为视为可能影响后续结果的暴露因素。通过纵向追踪智能体，该方法能够研究不良事件的行为决定因素，在因果假设下估计其潜在可预防负担，并刻画智能体工作生涯中行为变化的特征。
tldr: 本文借鉴人类流行病学队列研究方法，提出将AI智能体视为队列成员进行纵向追踪的评估框架，用以研究智能体不良事件的行为决定因素及其可预防负担。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an epidemiologic cohort design for agentic AI that treats agents as cohort members tracked longitudinally, enabling investigation of behavioral determinants of adverse events and estimation of their preventable burden.
